name: Socinians / Polish Brethren

facts.value: 1570, settled at Raków. Antitrinitarian circles from the 1540s

citations.excerpt: In 1570 the Socinians separated, and, through the influence of the Antitrinitarian John Sigismund, established themselves at Racow.
In 1546 a secret society held meetings at Vicenza in the Diocese of Venice to discuss, among other points, the doctrine of the Trinity.

facts.value: Lelio Sozzini and his nephew Fausto Sozzini

citations.excerpt: The Socinians derive their name from two natives of Siena , Lelio Sozzini (1525-62) and his nephew Fausto Sozzini (1539-1604).

facts.value: Antitrinitarian. Only doctrines grasped by reason were accepted, as set out in the Racovian Catechism.

citations.excerpt: The body of doctrine held by one of the numerous Antitrinitarian sects to which the Reformation gave birth.
in the mouth of Socinian it meant that only those mysteries which reason can grasp are to be accepted.
In 1638 the Catholics in Poland insisted on the banishment of the Socinians, who were in consequence dispersed.

facts.value: Fausto Sozzini came to Poland in 1579 and gained a leading influence in the Minor (antitrinitarian) Church's synods.

citations.excerpt: Excluded at first by his views on baptism (which he regarded as applicable only to Gentile converts) from the Minor or anti-Trinitarian ChuTch (largely anabaptist), he acquired by degrees a predominant influence in its synods.
Meanwhile, Faustus Socinus had obtained possession of his uncle's papers and in 1579 came to Poland .

research_notes: End 1638 per CE 1913 only. Check ODCC for the later expulsion date commonly given; add as disagreement if sourced.
